Build a simulation model from an initial fit

Source: R/as-sim-model.R
as_sim_model.Rd

Turns the Cox models of an fit_initial() fit into a simevent::sim_model(), with simevent::sim_model_from_fits(), so data resembling the observed data can be simulated with simevent::simulate_events(), e.g. to check an estimator where the truth is known. The process types and limits are taken from the fit.

Usage

as_sim_model(fit, data)

Arguments

fit

An initial fit, as returned by fit_initial().

data

The data that fit was fitted to, to resample covariates from.

Value

A simevent::sim_model().

Details

Covariates are resampled from data, one row per individual. A process that a hazard depends on enters it as in the fit: a recurrent process as the indicators of at least 1, ..., max_count jumps, and any other as its number of jumps so far. A process that jumps at most once in the data (type "one_jump") can jump at most once in the simulation too.

Fits with an at_risk condition in a hazard_model(), or with event_time() covariates, are not supported.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("simevent", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- fit_initial(
    illness_death,
    models = list(
      hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),
      death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,
      censoring ~ biomarker
    ),
    tau = 1
  )
  model <- as_sim_model(fit, illness_death)
  simulated <- simevent::simulate_events(model, n = 500, seed = 1)
  head(simulated)
}
#> Key: <id>
#>       id      time   event   biomarker treatment illness
#>    <int>     <num>  <fctr>       <num>     <num>   <num>
#> 1:     1 0.1730469 illness  0.03797316         0       1
#> 2:     1 0.7092549   death  0.03797316         0       1
#> 3:     2 2.5093113   death  2.94325166         1       0
#> 4:     3 0.8452039 illness -0.17643927         1       1
#> 5:     3 0.9287521   death -0.17643927         1       1
#> 6:     4 1.2212702   death -2.16792215         0       0
